discovery: Development of the X-ray free-electron laser based on self-amplified spontaneous emission (SASE)

nominees.name: Claudio Pellegrini
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Jörg Rossbach
nominees.affiliation: University of Hamburg and DESY, Germany

motivation: X-ray free-electron lasers have turned the X-ray into a coherent, femtosecond, laser-like probe, increasing peak brilliance by about a billion times over synchrotrons. Pellegrini developed the high-gain SASE theory and proposed and led the effort toward a linac-driven X-ray FEL, which was realised as LCLS in 2009. Rossbach led the TESLA Test Facility/FLASH work that first demonstrated SASE lasing at short VUV and soft X-ray wavelengths, giving the key experimental proof and leading to the European XFEL. Ishikawa showed with SACLA that compact, reliable hard X-ray FELs are possible, which widened access worldwide. Together they created a new instrument class. It now allows single-shot structural biology, time-resolved chemistry and catalysis, warm dense matter studies and nonlinear X-ray optics, and it has changed experimental physics across many disciplines.
